approach: I followed the data-engineering-steps skill for DE-02. I fetched the contracted input feat.tasks through context_get to get a receipt. I also fetched the approved DE-01 output task.repo_access as background, because it records the Databricks and workspace-credential findings. org.permission_table is restricted and passed by reference only, so I did not open it. Its verdict for ap_pipeline comes from the step's tool view (tool:repo-access), which reports the permission table. For each Data Engineering task (TSK-01, TSK-02), I checked the files in its budget, its must-not-change list and its I/O against the need for any credential. As my own cross-check, I searched the ap_pipeline checkout for environment-variable, secret, token, password or credential references and found none. I don't cite that search in the output, because only the tool view and contracted items are receipted. The result is that no secret is required, none is granted, there is no gap and no access request is raised. Two non-blocking re-entry conditions are recorded: release of TSK-01 against the production feed, and later scheduling or notification steps. I used no connectors (api:osv and api:pypi don't apply) and wrote only the declared output.

SS-2 has a similar mismatch, but it is framed as a risk, so it is listed under improvements.
